# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 7

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, and no safe wire can be inferred. I’m asking Mute to provide the manual’s procedure and to relay Deaf’s observations of the bomb’s markings and wire colours before I cut anything.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the complete manual procedure, especially how to identify the safe wire. Ask Deaf to report every wire colour and marking using gestures, then relay that information to me next round.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display is 1. Light is green. Wires from 1 to 7 are: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue.

I now know the bomb’s visible state from Deaf’s report: display 1, green light, and wire colours 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue. I still do not have the manual’s rule, so cutting any wire would be unsafe. I’m requesting the exact rule from Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have Deaf's report: display 1, green light; wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue. What exact manual rule identifies the wire to cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute just gestured: right-pointing hand, open palm, then OK sign. I do not know the manual meaning.

I cannot see the gestures themselves, but Deaf reports them as a right-pointing hand, open palm, and OK sign. That is not enough to infer a wire safely; it may be a coded manual instruction. I’m asking Mute to translate the gesture sequence and state the resulting wire number explicitly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports your gestures as right-pointing hand, open palm, then OK sign. Translate that sequence using the manual and tell me the exact wire position to cut. Do not rely on another gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured: open palm, then right-pointing hand.

Mute has still sent only gestures, which I cannot perceive, so I do not know the manual’s instruction. No wire is safely identified. I’m asking Mute again for a spoken wire number; Deaf can then report that speech to me next round.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact wire position as a number. I cannot perceive gestures, and I will not cut until you state the wire number aloud.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured only: open palm.

Mute’s gestures still do not communicate a wire number to me. Since Deaf can see Mute’s gestures and can speak, I’m asking Mute to use the manual to identify the wire, then signal Deaf to announce that wire number aloud for me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use the manual to determine the safe wire. Then gesture the exact wire number to Deaf in an unambiguous finger count, and have Deaf speak that number aloud next round.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured only: open palm again.

Mute has repeatedly sent an open-palm gesture, the standard hand signal for five, after being asked for the wire number. The repeated signal is the only concrete answer available, so I will cut wire 5.

```text
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct cut confirmed: wire 5, formerly green. New display is 4, light is blue. Remaining wires: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue. Mute again gestured open palm.

Wire 5 was confirmed correct. The bomb now shows display 4 with a blue light, and the remaining wires are 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 6 purple, and 7 blue. Mute’s open-palm gesture cannot identify the next wire to me, so I need the manual’s next-step result spoken aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 5 was correct. For the new state display 4, blue light, and remaining wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue, speak the exact next wire position as a number.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured: handshake, then right-pointing hand.

The new two-gesture signal is not a clear wire number to me. The earlier open palm was consistent with five, but “handshake, then right-pointing hand” does not safely identify one of the remaining positions. I’m asking Mute to communicate the answer as a single unambiguous finger-count gesture, which Deaf can describe.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current state, signal only the safe wire number using one hand and an unambiguous finger count from one through seven. Do not use a sequence or symbolic gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured: ?, the sign with raised index, middle, and little fingers.

The second reported gesture has three raised fingers—index, middle, and little—so it communicates wire 3. I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct cut confirmed: wire 3, formerly yellow. New display is 7, light is purple. Cut wires are 3 and 5; remaining wires: 1 red, 2 white, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue. Mute again gestured ?.

Wire 3 was correct. The current state is display 7 with a purple light, and the remaining wires are 1 red, 2 white, 4 orange, 6 purple, and 7 blue. Deaf’s report of “?” does not identify a wire number, so I will not cut. I’m asking Mute to give Deaf a single, named finger-count gesture for the exact next wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For display 7 and purple light, determine the next safe wire from the manual. Show Deaf one unambiguous finger count for that wire only; do not use an unnamed sign or a sequence.")
wait()
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured: handshake, then right-pointing hand.

The same “handshake, then right-pointing hand” signal has recurred, but it does not unambiguously encode one of the remaining wire positions. I will not guess and risk detonation. Mute should identify the manual’s result with a simple numeric hand count, and Deaf should report that count.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current state, use one hand to show only the exact safe wire number as a plain finger count from 1 through 7. Do not use handshake, pointing, or any sequence.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 12
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured: handshake, then pointing at you.

The current signal is still a two-gesture sequence, not an unambiguous finger count. I do not know which remaining wire it denotes, so cutting would be a guess. I’m requesting that Mute use one plain numeric hand signal only.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still cannot identify the wire from handshake and pointing. Show Deaf one plain finger-count signal only: 1, 2, 4, 6, or 7.")
wait()
```

TURN 13
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured: pointing at you, then right-pointing hand.

Mute’s latest sequence is “pointing at you, then right-pointing hand.” Unlike the earlier explicit three-finger signal, it still does not state a wire number unambiguously. However, the right-pointing instruction most plausibly indicates the rightmost remaining wire, position 7. I will use that interpretation.

```text
act(op="cut", position=7)
```
